what_its_for: Desonide is a mild steroid cream, ointment, foam, or lotion that helps relieve redness, itching, swelling, and irritation caused by skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, allergic reactions, and other inflammatory skin problems.
how_to_take: Wash and dry the affected skin area gently before applying. Apply a thin layer of desonide to the affected area and rub it in gently. Do not use more than your doctor prescribed. Do not cover the treated area with bandages or wraps unless your doctor tells you to. Wash your hands after applying unless you are treating your hands. Keep this medicine away from your eyes, mouth, and inside your nose.
dosing: Usually applied 2 to 3 times a day, or as directed by your doctor. Use the smallest amount that helps your symptoms. Do not use it for longer than your doctor recommends, as long-term use of steroids on the skin can cause side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep the lid or cap tightly closed. Keep out of reach of children. Do not freeze the product. Throw away any unused medication after your treatment is finished or after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not apply to your face, underarms, or groin area unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes or mouth. Do not use on broken, infected, or open skin unless directed by your doctor. Do not use more than prescribed or for a longer time than recommended. Avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants on children being treated in the diaper area, as this can increase absorption of the medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice skin thinning, stretch marks, easy bruising, or increased hair growth on the treated area. Call your doctor if your skin condition does not improve after 2 weeks of treatment, or if it gets worse. Also call if you develop signs of a skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, or oozing. If you accidentally get this in your eyes and notice irritation, rinse with water and contact your doctor.
when_it_works: Many people notice some improvement in redness and itching within a few days of starting treatment. Full improvement may take 1 to 2 weeks. If you do not see any improvement after 2 weeks, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Use with extra caution in children as they absorb more of this medicine through the skin than adults, which can affect growth. Use only as directed and for the shortest time needed. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. It should only be used if clearly necessary and in small amounts. Elderly patients: Use with caution as older skin may be more sensitive to the effects of steroids.
